inputs.content: I'm comparing three cloud storage providers for my photography business: Google Drive (2TB for $9.99/mo), Dropbox Professional (3TB for $19.99/mo), and Sync.com (2TB for $8/mo). I need a side-by-side feature table, which is cheapest, and a recommendation since I work with large RAW files and need fast upload speeds for client delivery.

Here's your comparison table:

| Feature | Google Drive 2TB | Dropbox Professional 3TB | Sync.com 2TB |
|---------|------------------|--------------------------|--------------|
| Price/mo | $9.99 | $19.99 | $8.00 |
| Storage | 2 TB | 3 TB | 2 TB |
| Max file size | 5 TB | 2 TB | Unlimited |
| Upload speed | Good (varies by region) | Excellent (block-level sync) | Good |
| Zero-knowledge encryption | No | No | Yes |
| File versioning | 30 days | 180 days | 365 days |
| Sharing controls | Basic | Advanced (passwords, expiry) | Advanced |
| Mobile app | Excellent | Excellent | Good |

**Cheapest: Sync.com at $8/month**

**Recommendation for your RAW file workflow: Go with Dropbox Professional.** Despite being the priciest, its block-level sync (only uploading changed portions of files) dramatically speeds up RAW file uploads — critical when you're delivering 50+ GB galleries to clients on deadline. The 3TB also gives you headroom for multiple active projects. Sync.com's encryption is great for privacy but adds overhead that slows large transfers. Google Drive is fine for general use but lacks the sync optimization you need.

Looking at three email marketing platforms for my bakery: MailerLite (1,000 subs for $10/mo), ConvertKit (1,000 subs for $29/mo), and Brevo (unlimited contacts, 300 emails/day free tier). Please give me a feature comparison table, highlight the cheapest option, and recommend one for a small bakery that sends weekly newsletters with photos and occasional promo blasts for holidays.

Here's your comparison:

| Feature | MailerLite | ConvertKit | Brevo (free tier) |
|---------|------------|------------|-------------------|
| Monthly cost (1k subs) | $10 | $29 | $0 (300 emails/day limit) |
| Contact limit | 1,000 | 1,000 | Unlimited |
| Email limit/mo | Unlimited | Unlimited | 9,000 |
| Automation | Basic | Advanced | Basic |
| Landing pages | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Drag-drop editor | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| RSS-to-email | Yes | Yes | No |
| Deliverability reputation | Good | Excellent | Good |
| Support | Email/chat | Email/chat (priority >$50) | Email only |

**Cheapest: Brevo free tier** (if you stay under 300 emails/day / 9k/month). Otherwise MailerLite at $10/month.

Both MailerLite and Brevo's free tier will handle your weekly newsletter + holiday promos comfortably. MailerLite's automation is more visual if you want to set up a welcome sequence for new subscribers.

We're a 12-person fully remote design agency choosing between Asana (Premium $13.49/user/mo), Monday.com (Standard $12/user/mo, 3-user min), and ClickUp (Unlimited $7/user/mo). Need a feature table, cheapest callout, and a recommendation — we run 30+ concurrent client projects, need time tracking for billing, and our team hates cluttered interfaces.

Comparison table:

| Feature | Asana Premium | Monday.com Standard | ClickUp Unlimited |
|---------|---------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Price/user/mo | $13.49 | $12.00 | $7.00 |
| Min seats | 1 | 3 | 1 |
| Monthly cost (12 users) | $1,942.56 | $1,728.00 | $1,008.00 |
| Time tracking | Native (Premium+) | Native (Pro+) | Native |
| Custom fields | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Gantt/timeline | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Workload view | Yes | Yes (Pro+) | Yes |
| Automations/mo | 25,000 | 250 actions | 1,000 |
| Interface density | Clean, list-focused | Visual, board-heavy | Highly customizable |
| Mobile app | Excellent | Good | Good |
| Guest access | Free | Free | Free |

**Cheapest: ClickUp at $1,008/month for 12 users**

**Recommendation: Asana Premium.** Your team hates clutter — Asana's cleaner, list-first interface reduces cognitive load compared to Monday's busy boards or ClickUp's endless customization options (which become clutter fast). Native time tracking works well for billing, and the 25k automations/month handles recurring project setup across 30+ concurrent clients. ClickUp's price is tempting but its flexibility backfires with teams that want opinionated defaults. Monday's 3-seat minimum isn't an issue but its visual density frustrates clutter-averse users.

Digital nomad here comparing VPNs: Mullvad (€5/mo flat), ProtonVPN Plus (€9.99/mo), and IVPN (Standard $6/mo, Pro $10/mo). I need a feature table, which is cheapest, and a recommendation for someone who works from cafes in Southeast Asia, needs reliable WireGuard speeds for video calls, and values no-logs verification.

VPN comparison:

| Feature | Mullvad | ProtonVPN Plus | IVPN Standard |
|---------|---------|----------------|---------------|
| Monthly price | €5 (~$5.40) | €9.99 (~$10.80) | $6.00 |
| Protocols | WireGuard, OpenVPN | WireGuard, OpenVPN, Stealth | WireGuard, OpenVPN |
| Servers/Countries | 600+/40 | 3,000+/70 | 100+/30 |
| No-logs audit | Yes (2022, 2023) | Yes (2022, 2023) | Yes (2022, 2023) |
| Port forwarding | Yes | No | Yes (Pro only) |
| Multi-hop | Yes | Yes (Secure Core) | Yes |
| Simultaneous connections | 5 | 10 | 7 |
| Payment options | Crypto, cash, card | Crypto, card | Crypto, card |
| Diskless RAM-only servers | No | Yes | No |

**Cheapest: Mullvad at €5/month**

Mullvad's flat pricing, WireGuard support, and audited no-logs policy make it a strong baseline. ProtonVPN's Secure Core multi-hop adds extra protection if you're on sketchy cafe WiFi. IVPN's Standard tier covers the basics well.

Freelance dev choosing accounting software: Wave (free), QuickBooks Online Simple Start ($30/mo), and Xero Early ($15/mo). Need feature table, cheapest, and a recommendation — I have 15-20 clients/year, need invoicing with late fee automation, bank reconciliation, and Schedule C export for US taxes.

Accounting software comparison:

| Feature | Wave (Free) | QuickBooks Simple Start | Xero Early |
|---------|-------------|-------------------------|------------|
| Monthly cost | $0 | $30 | $15 |
| Invoicing | Unlimited | Unlimited | 20/month |
| Late fee automation | No | Yes | Yes |
| Bank feeds | Yes (limited banks) | Yes (extensive) | Yes (extensive) |
| Bank reconciliation | Manual matching | Assisted | Assisted |
| Schedule C export | No (manual) | Yes | Yes (via reports) |
| Multi-currency | No | Yes (Essentials+) | Yes |
| Receipt capture | Mobile app | Mobile app | Mobile app |
| Accountant access | Free | Free | Free |
| Payroll add-on | No | $45+/mo | $39+/mo |

**Cheapest: Wave (free)**

**Recommendation: Xero Early at $15/month.** Wave's lack of late fee automation and Schedule C export means you'll spend hours each tax season manually compiling data — not worth the $15 savings. QuickBooks Simple Start is overkill at $30 for a solo dev. Xero Early hits your sweet spot: 20 invoices/month covers your 15-20 clients, late fee automation chases payments, assisted bank rec saves hours, and Schedule C data exports cleanly via the Tax Preparation report. Upgrade to Growing ($37) only if you exceed 20 invoices.

Local restaurant owner comparing website builders: Wix (Core $29/mo), Squarespace (Business $33/mo), and WordPress.com (Business $40/mo + hosting). Need a feature table, cheapest option highlighted, and a recommendation for a restaurant that needs online ordering integration, menu management, reservation widgets, and easy photo updates for daily specials.

Website builder comparison for your restaurant:

| Feature | Wix Core | Squarespace Business | WordPress.com Business |
|---------|----------|----------------------|------------------------|
| Monthly cost | $29 | $33 | $40 + hosting (~$10) |
| Online ordering | Wix Restaurants (incl.) | Squarespace Commerce (3% fee) | WooCommerce (free plugin) |
| Menu management | Dedicated menu app | Product blocks | WooCommerce products |
| Reservation widgets | OpenTable, Resy integrations | Acuity, OpenTable | Many plugins (OpenTable, etc.) |
| Photo/gallery updates | Drag-drop, easy | Drag-drop, easy | Block editor, more steps |
| Mobile editor | Yes | Yes | Limited |
| Transaction fees | 2.9% + $0.30 | 3% (on Commerce) | 2.9% + $0.30 (Stripe) |
| SSL, domain | Included | Included | Included |

**Cheapest: Wix Core at $29/month**

Wix's dedicated restaurant apps (Menus, Orders, Reservations) are purpose-built and integrate natively. Squarespace's Commerce plan works but charges 3% transaction fees on top of payment processing. WordPress.com gives you maximum control via WooCommerce but has a steeper learning curve for daily menu/specials updates.

Real estate agent comparing CRMs: Follow Up Boss ($69/user/mo), LionDesk ($32/user/mo), and Realvolve ($50/user/mo). Need feature table, cheapest, and a recommendation — solo agent, 50-60 transactions/year, need automated drip campaigns for buyer/seller leads, transaction management with compliance docs, and mobile app that works well at open houses.

Real estate CRM comparison:

| Feature | Follow Up Boss | LionDesk | Realvolve |
|---------|----------------|----------|-----------|
| Price/user/mo | $69 | $32 | $50 |
| Annual cost (solo) | $828 | $384 | $600 |
| Drip campaigns | Excellent (Smart Plans) | Good (Workflows) | Excellent (Workflows) |
| Transaction mgmt | Basic (checklists) | Basic | Strong (compliance-focused) |
| Compliance docs storage | Limited | Limited | Native (broker review ready) |
| Mobile app | Excellent (iOS/Android) | Good | Good |
| Open house check-in | Native (Kiosk mode) | QR code forms | Manual entry |
| Lead routing/pond | Yes (teams) | No | No |
| Integrations | 250+ (Zapier, MLS) | 100+ | 50+ |
| Dialer/texting | Built-in ($) | Built-in ($) | Via integration |

**Cheapest: LionDesk at $384/year**

**Recommendation: Follow Up Boss at $69/month.** For a solo agent doing 50-60 deals, the open house Kiosk mode alone saves hours of manual lead entry every weekend — leads scan a QR code, enter info, and land directly in a buyer drip campaign. Smart Plans are the most polished drip system for nurturing both buyer and seller leads long-term. LionDesk's lower price shows in its clunkier mobile experience and weaker transaction tracking. Realvolve's compliance strength matters more for teams with broker oversight. The $444/year premium over LionDesk pays for itself in 2-3 captured open house leads.

High school teacher comparing video conferencing for hybrid classes: Zoom One Pro ($15.99/mo), Google Workspace Teaching & Learning ($12/user/mo, 50 min limit on free), and Microsoft Teams for Education (free for schools, paid add-ons). Need feature table, cheapest, and a recommendation — I teach 5 classes of 25-30 students, need breakout rooms, polling, attendance reports, and LMS integration with Canvas.

Video conferencing for education:

| Feature | Zoom One Pro | Google Workspace T&L | MS Teams for Education |
|---------|--------------|----------------------|------------------------|
| Cost (individual) | $15.99/mo | $12/mo (or free 50 min) | Free (school license) |
| Meeting duration | 30 hours | 24 hours (paid) / 50 min (free) | Unlimited |
| Max participants | 100 | 250 | 300 |
| Breakout rooms | Yes (50 rooms) | Yes (paid) | Yes |
| Polling/quizzes | Advanced | Basic (Forms) | Forms integration |
| Attendance reports | Yes | Yes | Yes (Insights) |
| Canvas LMS integration | LTI Pro (paid add-on) | Native (Google Classroom) | Native (Teams meetings) |
| Recording storage | 5 GB cloud | 100 GB (paid) | 1 TB (OneDrive) |
| Whiteboard | Yes | Jamboard | Whiteboard |

**Cheapest: Microsoft Teams for Education (free with school license)**

If your school has a Microsoft 365 license, Teams is free and covers breakout rooms, polls via Forms, attendance via Insights, and native Canvas integration. Zoom's LTI Pro add-on for Canvas costs extra. Google's free tier has the 50-minute limit which breaks 90-minute block schedules.

Etsy seller comparing payment processors: Shopify Payments (2.9% + $0.30, Shopify only), Stripe (2.9% + $0.30), and Square (2.6% + $0.10 online). Need feature table, cheapest per-transaction, and a recommendation — I sell $15-40 handmade ceramics, process 200-300 orders/month, need instant deposits, automatic sales tax calculation for 15 states, and easy refunds for damaged-in-transit items.

Payment processor comparison:

| Feature | Shopify Payments | Stripe | Square |
|---------|------------------|--------|--------|
| Online rate | 2.9% + $0.30 | 2.9% + $0.30 | 2.6% + $0.10 |
| Monthly fee | $0 (with Shopify plan) | $0 | $0 |
| Instant deposits | 1-2 days (Shopify Balance) | Instant (1% fee) | Instant (1.5% fee) |
| Sales tax calc (15 states) | Shopify Tax (incl.) | Stripe Tax (0.5%/txn) | Square Tax (incl.) |
| Refunds | Full fee returned | Fee not returned | Fee not returned |
| Chargeback protection | Shopify Protect (elig.) | Radar (paid) | Square Chargeback Protection |
| POS integration | Shopify POS | Via terminal | Native (Square POS) |
| Payout schedule | Daily | Daily/rolling | Next business day |

**Cheapest per-transaction: Square at 2.6% + $0.10**

**Recommendation: Stripe with Stripe Tax.** Square's lower rate saves ~$0.35 on a $25 order, but Stripe Tax's 0.5%/transaction handles your 15-state nexus automatically with roof-level accuracy — Square Tax only covers marketplace states. Stripe's instant deposits (1% fee) get you cash same-day for kiln/firing costs. Refunds don't return fees on any platform, but Stripe's partial refund API lets you deduct shipping for damaged items cleanly. Shopify Payments locks you into Shopify; you're on Etsy. The $0.35/order savings vs. Square isn't worth losing automated multi-state tax compliance.

Growing startup (40 employees, scaling to 80) comparing HRIS: BambooHR (~$8/emp/mo + $12 base), Gusto Complete ($40 base + $12/emp/mo), and Rippling ($35 base + $8/emp/mo). Need feature table, cheapest at current and projected headcount, and a recommendation — we need automated onboarding/offboarding, benefits admin for 3 medical plans, time-off tracking with accruals, and API access for our custom internal tools.

HRIS comparison for your startup:

| Feature | BambooHR | Gusto Complete | Rippling |
|---------|----------|----------------|----------|
| Base fee/mo | ~$12 | $40 | $35 |
| Per-employee/mo | ~$8 | $12 | $8 |
| Current cost (40) | ~$332 | $520 | $355 |
| Projected cost (80) | ~$652 | $1,000 | $675 |
| Automated onboarding | Yes (tasks, e-sign) | Yes (offer letters, docs) | Yes (device/app provisioning) |
| Offboarding workflows | Yes | Basic | Yes (device recovery, app revoke) |
| Benefits admin (3 plans) | Yes (open enrollment) | Yes (broker integration) | Yes (carrier connections) |
| Time-off accruals | Yes (custom policies) | Yes | Yes (custom policies) |
| API access | Yes (REST, webhooks) | Limited (partner only) | Yes (robust, well-documented) |
| Payroll integration | Via partners | Native (core strength) | Native |
| Device management | No | No | Yes (MDM) |

**Cheapest now: BambooHR (~$332/mo). Cheapest at 80: BambooHR (~$652/mo).**

BambooHR wins on price and covers your core HR needs. Rippling's API is superior for custom tooling. Gusto's payroll is best-in-class if you want unified HR+payroll.
